title: One Dead Whale Feeds the Deep Sea for 50 Years

scenes.text: A dead whale feeds the deep sea for fifty years.
It sinks kilometres to the seabed, and the feast begins.
Sleeper sharks and hagfish strip the blubber and muscle first.
Then worms, found in 2002, dissolve the bones using acid.
At least a hundred species have been found living on whale falls.
One body. Fifty years of dinner.

description:
When a whale dies and sinks, its body becomes a deep-sea habitat called a whale fall.
Scavengers eat the flesh, bone-eating Osedax worms, first found in 2002, dissolve the skeleton, and bacteria feed on what's left, sustaining hundreds of animals for up to 50 years.
Which part of the whale fall would you want to see in person? Comment below.
first_comment: The bone-eating worms were found in 2002 on a gray whale carcass nearly 3,000 metres down near Monterey. Would you dive down to see one?
